about: How the owner's chats get connected to Multi Auto Setup, as data. Each host lists its steps per operating system; the code that runs a step is generic (src/envrec_coordinator/connect.py) and never knows a host by name. A cell that is not documented for an operating system refuses with a typed reason instead of guessing. Every path and flag below is quoted from the tool's own documentation (see `sources`).

claude-desktop.label: Claude Desktop
claude-desktop.quits_to_edit: Claude Desktop rewrites its settings file when it quits, so it must be fully quit (Cmd+Q on macOS) before the file is edited, and started again afterwards.

steps.title: Keep a copy of the settings file
Add the multi-auto-setup entry to the settings file
Read the settings file back and check the entry

claude-desktop.verification: the settings file is read back and our entry is found

steps.title: Add the MCP server with the claude command
Check that claude lists the server
steps.name: multi-auto-setup

codex.label: Codex

steps.title: Keep a copy of the settings file
Add the multi-auto-setup table to the settings file
Read the settings file back and check the table

codex.verification: the settings file is read back and our table is found

opencode.label: OpenCode

windows.text: OpenCode's documentation gives the global settings location only as ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json and does not say where it is on Windows.

steps.title: Keep a copy of the settings file
Add the multi-auto-setup entry under mcp in the settings file
Read the settings file back and check the entry

opencode.verification: the settings file is read back and our entry is found

muse-code.label: Muse Code

windows.text: Muse Code's documentation gives the settings file as $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/muse/settings.json or ~/.config/muse/settings.json and does not say where it is on Windows.

steps.title: Keep a copy of the settings file
Add the multi-auto-setup entry under mcpServers in the settings file
Read the settings file back and check the entry

muse-code.verification: the settings file is read back and our entry is found

openwebui.label: Open WebUI
sources: https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui (the pinned version's own source: env.py, utils/auth.py create_admin_user, routers/functions.py)
openwebui.license_exception: Open WebUI License (BSD-3-style plus a branding clause), which is not on the MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD or ISC list. Open WebUI is a separate tool: it is not bundled, modified or redistributed, and its branding is left as it is. Approving the install accepts this exception.

steps.title: Make Open WebUI's own folder
Create a Python environment there and install the pinned Open WebUI
Start Open WebUI on this computer only, offline, with a first admin account
Add our function to Open WebUI through its own API, turn it on and set its valve
Ask Open WebUI whether the function is there, on, and has its valve

openwebui.verification: the function is read back from Open WebUI's own API and found on, with its valve set

openwebui-cleanup.label: Remove the manual Open WebUI install
sources: https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui (the server this plan stops is the one started from the folder named in the plan; nothing else is touched)

steps.title: Stop the Open WebUI server that was started from that folder
Move that folder aside (nothing is deleted)
Check that the folder moved and nothing of it is running

openwebui-cleanup.verification: the folder is found at its new name, is gone from its old place, and no server started from it is running
openwebui-cleanup.plan_title: Plan to remove the manual Open WebUI install from this computer

launcher._note: How a chat host starts our MCP server. When this program runs from an install, the host is pointed at the installer's `mas` command (it follows `mas update`, so the entry never names a release folder); from a source checkout it is the running interpreter running the package. Paths are per operating system, as data.
launcher.shim_mark: written by the Multi Auto Setup installer

_entry_markers_note: An entry under our name whose command or arguments contain one of these is an earlier version of OUR entry and is replaced (with the file copied first, and the old entry kept for the undo). Any other entry under our name is somebody else's and is never touched.
